strategy.evidence_chain: Profile evidence: baseline qwen_tp2 T=1 passes at 1438.912 us. Code evidence: fused_moe_kernel.cu launches stage1 over (T*TOPK,I), stage2 over (T*TOPK,H,split), and each element repeatedly decodes global_expert_raw and local range checks. Reference evidence: the SM120 MoE data-prep recipe builds expert_offsets/problem_sizes/a_map/c_map from topk_ids, uses single-CTA for topk_length <= 32768, and documents that CUB radix sort regressed while per-CTA offsets avoid hot global atomics. Inference: the baseline has no FlashInfer-style grouped expert metadata, so grouped GEMM children cannot get contiguous per-expert work. Action: build the missing expert-major schedule first, with a small-token fast path.
strategy.expected_impact: Creates the structural precondition for grouped GEMM and removes repeated per-output expert decoding from later kernels. On larger prefill token counts it should reduce launch-side and scatter overhead; on the current T=1 run the impact may be modest, but it should improve MAP-Elites diversity and make downstream compute rewrites simpler.
strategy.risks: For T=1/top_k=10, scheduling overhead can dominate if implemented as multiple kernels. Keep a single-CTA fast path and fall back to the parent staged kernels if the generated metadata mismatches the reference. Preserve Qwen TP2 local_expert_offset/local_num_experts semantics and avoid changing routing probabilities.
